#+title: Squeezed states
#+summary: The squeeze operator \(S(\xi)=e^{\frac12(\xi^*a^2-\xi a^{\dagger2})}\), \(\xi=re^{i\theta}\), reduces one quadrature to \(\tfrac12e^{-r}\) at the expense of the other \(\tfrac12e^{r}\); generated by degenerate parametric amplification, it beats the shot-noise limit in interferometers such as LIGO.

* Definition
\(S^\dagger aS=a\cosh r-a^\dagger e^{i\theta}\sinh r\). For \(\theta=0\), the rotated quadratures of \(\ket{\alpha,\xi}=D(\alpha)S(\xi)\ket0\) have
\[ \Delta X_1=\tfrac12e^{-r},\qquad \Delta X_2=\tfrac12e^{r},\qquad \Delta X_1\Delta X_2=\tfrac14. \]
Squeezing in dB: \(10\log_{10}e^{2r}\). Squeezed vacuum contains only even photon numbers, with \(\bar n=\sinh^2r\).

* Generation (derivation)
A \(\chi^{(2)}\) crystal pumped at \(2\omega\) gives the interaction \(H=i\hbar\frac\kappa2(a^{\dagger2}e^{-i\phi}-a^2e^{i\phi})\) (the pump is classical): its evolution operator is exactly \(S(\xi)\) with \(r=\kappa t\). Physically, photon pairs created together correlate the noise of the two sidebands \(\omega\pm\Omega\). In a cavity (OPO below threshold) the output squeezing spectrum is \(S_-(\Omega)=1-\frac{4\eta x}{(1+x)^2+(\Omega/\gamma)^2}\), \(x\) the pump parameter.

* Worked example
LIGO injects \(\sim\)6 dB of measured squeezing: shot-noise amplitude falls by \(10^{-6/20}=0.5\), i.e. sensitivity gains a factor 2 at high frequency, equivalent to 4× laser power without the extra thermal load. Losses \(\eta\) degrade squeezing as \(V=\eta e^{-2r}+(1-\eta)\): with 30% loss even infinite squeezing gives at most 5.2 dB.

* Engineering applications
Gravitational-wave detectors (frequency-dependent squeezing), quantum-enhanced microscopy and magnetometry, Josephson parametric amplifiers squeezing microwave fields for qubit read-out, continuous-variable quantum computing.

* Pitfall
Squeezing is fragile against loss: any attenuation mixes in vacuum noise. Squeezed light needs low-loss optics and high-efficiency photodiodes.
